name: CT-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joe Courtney holds a large money edge: about $603,000 on hand versus $125,000 for George Austin
District leans Democratic by four points and the national environment favors Democrats this cycle
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
No public general-election polling or expert ratings; challenger's fundraising is modest but nontrivial
model.rationale: Courtney combines incumbency, a four-point Democratic district lean, a favorable environment, and a roughly five-to-one cash advantage, while markets price his reelection near certain. With no polling or ratings signaling vulnerability, there is no basis to move off the fundamentals-driven picture.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Courtney or surprise polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signals to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Connecticut's Second District leans Democratic, and incumbent Joe Courtney returns with a clear financial advantage. He has raised about $760,000 and holds roughly $600,000 on hand, while Republican George Austin has brought in about $314,000 with $125,000 available. Outside spending is minimal on both sides. No public general-election polls are available and no major expert raters have ranked the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent, consistent with the district's four-point Democratic lean and a national environment favoring the party this cycle. Courtney has not faced a close contest in recent cycles, and the challenger's fundraising, while respectable for a first-time candidate, is unlikely to close the gap on its own. The seat sits in the Safe Democratic column, with any surprise most likely to come from late outside spending or an unexpected polling shift.
